subject: Draft: ephemeral prompt retention & derived-model access — DPA language proposal
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@crescenthealthtech.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Crescent HealthTech Legal <legal@crescenthealthtech.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA language request — ephemeral prompt retention and derived-model access

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security and legal teams asked us to pull together a concrete amendment to your standard DPA that covers two items before procurement can sign:

1) Ephemeral prompt retention: we need language that states prompts and user inputs are stored no longer than 14 days in production telemetry and are purged from any hot caches and non-transient logs. We also want an operational definition of what you consider "ephemeral" for telemetry and for debugging traces.

2) Derived-model access: CRITICAL — we need a clear, contractual assurance that Crescent HealthTech data will not be used to update or fine-tune any general-purpose or public models, nor to create derivative models accessible to third parties. We also need to understand the exceptions for anomaly investigations and how evidence of non-derivative processing would be provided.

Can you send proposed clause text, a short ops playbook for how you implement ephemeral deletion, and any evidence artifacts (audit log examples or deletion runbooks)? Our timeline is tight: legal would like a draft by EOD Friday (Dec 25) to circulate for exec review.

Attachments: none in this message.

— Marta
Marta Ruiz
Head of Security Programs
Crescent HealthTech
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@crescenthealthtech.com>
Cc: Crescent HealthTech Legal <legal@crescenthealthtech.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA language request — ephemeral prompt retention and derived-model access

Marta — thanks, and appreciated the clear asks. Attaching a first-pass clause and a short ops summary. High level:

- Ephemeral prompt retention: Redwood will retain customer prompt/interaction payloads in production telemetry for debugging and quality for a maximum of 14 days unless the customer enables a longer retention for explicit debugging sessions. We will:
  * purge hot KV/prefix caches within 24 hours after session termination;
  * delete stored telemetry records from primary logs within 14 days using automated deletion workflows;
  * mark any backups that might include telemetry for expedited deletion on the same schedule and provide a deletion confirmation record.

- Derived-model access: Redwood will not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, evaluate, or otherwise improve any model or model variant that is externally accessible. Exceptions: ephemeral replays or isolated synthetic reproductions used only by the customer and for internal incident response require prior written approval.

What I am attaching: proposed_dpa_ephemeral_clause_v1.docx (clause + short implementation notes) and our SFTP onboarding checklist (for customers that require export copies).

Actions I need from our side: David — can you prepare a 1-page ops runbook that describes the deletion job (cron, verification, audit events) and provide a sanitized sample audit event? Kimberly — please confirm KMS/keystore routing options for Crescent (onshore EU KMS vs Redwood-managed keys) and whether a zero-retention debug mode is feasible for their plan.

I’ll flag that legal timeline; Friday EOD is tight but we can aim to deliver the clause and ops summary by Thursday EOD.

Thanks — Avery
Avery Johnson
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 13:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA language request — ephemeral prompt retention and derived-model access

Avery / Kimberly — drafting a concise ops runbook now. Key technical points I'll include:

- Data plane retention layers:
  * Runtime caches (in-GPU/KV): TTL enforced, explicit eviction on session end (typically < 24h).
  * Application telemetry (structured logs): retention policy = 14 days (configurable per customer but contractually capped unless customer opt-in).
  * Backups / snapshots: flagged and subject to expedited deletion; backups are immutable but we maintain a deletion index to ensure removal in the next maintenance window (I’ll include the expected max lag).

- Deletion verification: deletion job emits audit event (audit_id, timestamp, data_scope, retention_policy_applied). We can provide a redacted sample audit event (JSON with fields and timestamps).

- Incident exceptions: for incident response we can create a secure, time-limited sandbox that captures only requested session slices. Those sessions are accessible only to named Redwood engineers and are scoped to a maximum 72-hour retention unless customer provides written consent to extend.

I will attach a sanitized sample audit event and the runbook by end of day. Kimberly — please confirm the KMS options; if Crescent requires EU-managed keys with HSM controls, we have a Private option roadmap we can present.

— David
David Kim
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachments: sftp-onboard-checklist.pdf
From: Crescent HealthTech Legal <legal@crescenthealthtech.com>

Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 15:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA language request — ephemeral prompt retention and derived-model access

Thanks for the fast turnaround and for the attachments. A few follow-ups from our counsel after an initial read:

1) Can you expand the derived-model language to explicitly prohibit:
  - using Customer Data to generate or seed any public or shared models;
  - using Customer Data in any benchmark sets that might be redistributed;
  - creating derivative models that are not contractually exclusive to Crescent.

2) For the incident-response exception: we need the names/roles of Redwood staff who would be allowed to access time-limited sandboxes, and we require that access be recorded in tamper-evident audit logs with an approver stamp from Crescent. Is that supported?

3) KMS: Crescent prefers customer-managed keys hosted in the EU. Our procurement team has asked whether you can support a Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) flow for your Private deployment or, failing that, an onshore key escrow arrangement.

4) Evidence: legal would like a redacted example of the audit event you referenced, and they want to see the deletion job schedule (cron) and a sample deletion confirmation message as part of the packet.

Please send an updated clause with these specifics and the requested artifacts. If you can get a redline back by Thursday EOD (Dec 24) that would keep us on track for our internal signoff the following week.

Best,
Crescent HealthTech Legal
